probes.startupProbe: /health every 5s, failureThreshold 24 (2 min budget for a cold start)
probes.livenessProbe: /health every 20s - deliberately touches no dependency, so a dependency outage never restarts a healthy pod
probes.readinessProbe: /ready every 10s - fans out to dependencies; 503 drains the pod from the gateway

resilience.hpa: cpu 70% utilisation, min 2 / max 8, scaleDown stabilisation 300s

live_argocd_sync_and_self_heal.reason: No Kubernetes cluster is reachable from this machine. kubectl v1.29.2 is installed but kind, minikube, kustomize, helm and the argocd CLI are not, and `kubectl cluster-info` finds no server. Docker Desktop's built-in Kubernetes would need roughly the whole 7.6 GiB VM, of which the 14-container lab stack already holds about 6.3 GiB, so bringing up a cluster would mean tearing down the running platform and destroying the demo state this evidence pack depends on.
what_would_prove_it: argocd app sync lab28-platform, then argocd app get showing Synced/Healthy
kubectl -n lab28 set image deploy/lab28-api api=<other-tag> to inject drift, then argocd app get showing the field reverted by selfHeal
git revert of the tag commit, then argocd app history / argocd app rollback, then kubectl -n lab28 get deploy -o wide showing replicas and image back at 3.0.0
